questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is discouraged.
Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you better.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see better and be seen by others.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards in the road. Good positioning discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: To get the best protection, wear a helmet that:

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is well-worn and broken in.
Is pretty loose.
Does not have a chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Restricts your vision to the sides.
Can greatly reduce head and neck injuries.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head and neck injuries.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A good helmet will not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not fully cover your arms or legs.
Should not include a jacket if it is warm.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing provides vital protection in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap but be loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should completely cover your arms and legs.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.
Should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should completely cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should completely cover your arms and legs for protection. They should fit snugly but be loose enough to let you move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the impact.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs and joints absorb some of the force from the uneven surface. This prevents the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Is a useless action.
Lets the rider use engine braking.
Is illegal.
Should not be done if other vehicles are around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the rider use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting is a useful technique. If you use engine braking, apply your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Wear long pants.
Wear shorts if it is warm.
Wear loose-fitting clothing.
Wear sandals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear long pants.
questions.explanation: Wear pants and a jacket made of durable materials that completely cover your arms and legs. Exposed skin is at risk if you crash.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Help other drivers identify you.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
Offer no protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Why is a cushion of space helpful when riding?

options.text: It gives you time to react to hazards.
It hides you from other drivers.
It prevents you from avoiding hazards.
It allows you to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You will have room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What should proper motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Your arms and legs completely.
Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever is comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely for proper protection while riding.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Assume they have ridden a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
Do not let them ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Never assume they know what to do. Give complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?

options.text: Dirt or gravel road
Oil on the road
Mud on pavement
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. These include wet pavement, loose gravel, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, oil, and metal covers. Dry pavement provides the best grip for motorcycles.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: You should not wear them because your hands will get too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handgrips.
You should not wear them because they make controls harder to use.
You should only wear them on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handgrips.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the single most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Twice a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent dangerous problems before you ride.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
The effects are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
The effects are usually minor.
The effects usually balance out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can affect your riding ability. When combined with alcohol, some drugs become even more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes.
Bright-colored clothes.
Lights.
A black jacket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you. Choose clothes that make you visible during the day and at night.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left part of your lane before passing?

options.text: It helps you see ahead better.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It blocks your view of the vehicle ahead.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see ahead better.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see ahead and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.
